featured_reviews.name: Sheldon Dias
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in the St. Pauls Media Complex, St Paul Book And Art Centre Mumbai is a serene landmark that serves as a one-stop destination for spiritual literature and religious artifacts. It is particularly well-regarded for its peaceful, library-like atmosphere, offering a quiet refuge for visitors to browse through a wide range of specialized materials.
• Diverse Collection: The store is a major hub for religious and spiritual books, including Bibles in various editions, theological texts, and Catholic literature, as well as academic titles, CBSE textbooks, and children's storybooks.
• Art and Gifts: Beyond literature, it features an extensive selection of religious artifacts, such as statues, rosaries, candles, and framed prints, making it a popular spot for meaningful gifts and church supplies.
• Holiday Highlights: During the Christmas season, the first floor transforms into a festive destination stocked with unique décor, souvenirs, and seasonal ornaments.
• Supportive Environment: Visitors frequently mention the well-organized layout and the helpful, professional staff who are knowledgeable about the inventory and assist with niche title requests.

featured_reviews.name: Sara Epifanio
featured_reviews.review_text: Oh my, if this isn’t a special little place in all of Mumbai. Amazing curated selection of books (and some stationary) and the most welcoming team. Loved everything about it - including asking for a shop stamp on my purchases! Truly recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Samaira K
featured_reviews.review_text:
i've been a member here for a couple of years, with a break of a year or so in between. tucked away in the bylanes of carter road, this place is a quaint little gem! the library membership plans are well priced (i got a personal subscription at 2500 for 6 months) and the owners are always friendly and welcoming, in my experience. they also have a great comic book/graphic novel collection, which is a highlight as someone who adores reading them. and the bookstore gives a great discount to members and an excellent and unique collection, especially for artists and creative individuals- i have to keep reminding myself to finish the books i already have before going on another bookshop spree 🫠
i do admit the lane is hard to spot sometimes and can be crowded, but personally i don't mind since i'm used to it and the store and library are maintained very well. there's always some cosy jazz music on which adds to the warm atmosphere. overall, a brilliant place and an excellent way to spend your free time surrounded by great books!

featured_reviews.name: Megha
featured_reviews.review_text: A place that left me at a loss of words and utterly amazed. I'm so GLAD I visited it. One of the few bookshops that has taken the effort to make the shopping and reading experience, cohesive and meaningful for its readers. Very thoughtfully curated books and spatial arrangement.

featured_reviews.name: Meg Huber
featured_reviews.review_text: One of my favorite things to do while traveling is visit bookshops and this one did not disappoint! The books were well organized and the collection curated. I wondered upstairs and was happy to find that the lending library also has fantastic titles. I ended up buying three books but if my bag had more space I would have gotten more. I enjoyed perusing and spent lots of time picking up books reading about them and putting them down. I didn’t feel rushed in anyway.  The shop itself is down a very short ally and has a bright yellow sign making it easy to spot if you are looking for it.

featured_reviews.name: Abheet Sethi
featured_reviews.review_text:
First time visitor. Came to the store on the recommendation of a friend. The staff, namely Mithil and Ahalya, are very sweet, welcoming and patiently answered all questions I had. I purchased Rahul Bhattacharya 's Railsong and when I got home, I realized it's a signed copy! This was a very happy surprise!

The store may appear to be small but has a great collection going beyond the usual bestsellers we see at most larger book chains. If you're looking to explore new, less read titles, this is the place to go.

Also, the upstairs lending library has a large and diverse collection. If you live in Bandra/Khar and a serious reader, I reckon it's well worth becoming a susbscribing member. One cool thing is that members can also sit in the cosy upstairs library and read.

featured_reviews.name: Freya Dutta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Without a doubt the best book store in Bombay at this time. As a first time buyer, with no connections to the owners, we wandered in to Trilogy one afternoon with low expectations given our other experiences at book stores in Bombay (mostly mall stores, filled with pop sci, buisness books, religious books, or the same set of comics). However, we were pleasantly surprised! We left with too many books, some in Hindi (I'm working on improving my hindi, so thanks for that!), several indie comic books, and a delightful cross section of speculative fiction that I find myself returning to re-read often. We even found the perfect gift for my mom, a calendar fundraising for stray dogs and cats with the cutest pictures of indies and their doting humans in them. And yes, the owners are wonderful, and despite not knowing them before, we had a wonderful chat filled with useful recommendations curated to our tastes.

Book shops are for browsing, it's odd to see reviews criticising a book store encouraging buyers to physically engage with their books. I guess the amazon age makes people buy books only based on their covers, I hope the poor souls scared of touching books get over it and experience the joy of holding a book, turning it's pages and even relishing the smell of new books!

A must visit for anyone who dwells into nostalgia.

One of the finest comic book stores in Bandra with an amazing collection of Marvel and DC comics. From vintage classics to modern editions, the vibe itself feels like stepping into another era.

For Indian comics, pre-orders are recommended, but the collection and guidance make it absolutely worth it. A great spot for kids, collectors, and anyone who still believes superheroes shaped their childhood.

A hidden paradise for comic lovers in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Sampath Iyengarr
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited this comic book store on Linking Road, Bandra, and I’m thoroughly impressed! The selection of comics is incredible—from classic superhero issues to indie graphic novels—making it a true haven for comic enthusiasts. The staff, warm and knowledgeable, is always ready to suggest hidden gems based on your preferences. The layout is well organized, so it’s easy to find exactly what you’re looking for. I also appreciated the cozy reading corners where you can flip through your favorite issues. If you’re a comic book lover in Mumbai, this place is an absolute must-visit!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Then we walked into Crosswords bookstore right next door and realized Third Wave is inside the store, near the counter. There is a decent seating area there, not huge, but enough space to sit comfortably with a coffee.

The bookstore itself is nice. It’s spacious and has a wide range of books and other products. You’ll find books across many genres, along with stationery and gift items. Prices vary a lot. Some books are affordable, while others, especially imported editions, are quite expensive. It really depends on what you pick up and where it’s coming from.

I liked that there were options at different price points. You can browse without feeling rushed, and it doesn’t feel too cramped even when there are people around. The coffee inside makes it a good place to pause for a bit, read a few pages, or just sit quietly.

We were actually looking for Third Wave Coffee and found it on the map. When we reached the building, there was no sign of it anywhere. Nothing in the elevator either, so we were a bit confused at first

Overall, it’s a good bookstore to visit in Juhu if you enjoy browsing and don’t mind spending some time there. Just know that Third Wave Coffee is inside Crosswords and not a separate outlet, which can be confusing at first.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Granth Book Store in Juhu recently and honestly felt a little disappointed with the overall customer experience. A bookstore is usually expected to feel welcoming and comfortable for readers, but the staff behavior did not reflect that warmth.

While I was casually clicking pictures of the bookstore, one of the helpers stopped me and said photography was not allowed. What felt confusing was that the Google reviews of the same store already contain several visitor-clicked photos. If photography policies exist, they should at least be communicated politely and consistently.
Another uncomfortable part of the experience was the way the staff constantly observed us while we were browsing books, almost as if customers were being viewed with suspicion rather than trust. Browsing peacefully is one of the most enjoyable parts of visiting a bookstore, and unfortunately that comfort was missing here.
The bookstore itself has a lovely collection, which is why I genuinely hope the management works on creating a more welcoming and customer-friendly environment for book lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Naveed Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text: The Book Shop in Vile Parle East has been a quiet constant in my life for as long as I can remember. I’ve been visiting it since childhood, hand in hand with my father, when a good book and a peaceful afternoon felt like the perfect reward. Today, I walk those same paths with my wife, hoping that one day my child will do the same. There’s something timeless about this place—an old-world charm that refuses to fade. Books spill out onto the pavement, from classics and self-help to academic treasures, many of them second-hand and priced at a fraction of their worth. I’ve never walked away empty-handed; somehow, I always find a title that speaks to me. The affordability is a gift, especially when so much around us keeps getting more expensive. That said, I’ve heard whispers—and felt a hint myself—of the staff being a little curt or unwelcoming at times. It doesn’t happen often, but it’s there. Still, the connection I have with this shop runs deeper than a few words exchanged across a counter. It’s where stories begin—on paper and in life. And for that, I’ll always return.
